SecuVidyra Academy

Web and API Security Testing

For learners comfortable with HTTP, Linux and basic VAPT.
8 weeks: 32 live hours + 32 guided practice hours
Outcome: demonstrate skills through lab evidence and an individual submission.

Proposed schedule. Dates, fees and mode to be confirmed.

Learning modules:

Application mapping

Identify roles, workflows and trust boundaries.
Inventory endpoints and sensitive data.
Record expected access before testing.



HTTP and interception

Observe an approved request through a local proxy.
Keep an unchanged baseline for comparison.
Change one input at a time in the sandbox.



Authentication lifecycle

Review login, reset and account recovery.
Look for inconsistent identity checks.
Check error handling and rate limits safely.



Session management

Sessions should expire according to policy.
Logout should invalidate relevant server-side state.
Cookies need suitable security attributes.



Object-level authorisation

A valid user may still lack access to an object.
Verify ownership on every relevant request.
Compare two authorised test accounts.



Function and property permissions

Separate administrator functions from normal users.
Restrict sensitive properties during reads and writes.
Server-side checks must enforce the role model.



Injection and output encoding

Data must remain data at interpreter boundaries.
Parameterised queries reduce SQL injection risk.
Output encoding depends on the destination context.



CSRF and cross-origin policies

Browsers can attach credentials automatically.
State-changing actions need appropriate request protections.
CORS controls browser access to cross-origin responses.



Server-side requests and uploads

Outbound requests can cross internal boundaries.
Uploads require validation, safe storage and access controls.
Restrict destinations and avoid executable upload paths.



API tokens and claims

Validate token signature and intended context.
Enforce expiry and expected issuer/audience.
Keep signing keys and tokens out of logs.



Business logic and workflow

Security checks must follow the full business process.
Test invalid step order and repeated requests in a lab.
Use small, controlled examples for financial workflows.



API inventory and resource limits

Document versions and deprecated endpoints.
Apply suitable quotas and request-size limits.
Validate configuration without stressing a live service.



Coverage and evidence

Map each test to a role, endpoint and expected control.
Record pass, fail, blocked or not tested.
Explain exclusions and environment limits.



Developer-ready findings

Describe a minimal reproducible case.
State expected and observed behaviour.
Suggest a fix at the enforcement boundary.
Retest the original case and related roles.



Capstone

Test the fictional student portal with three roles.
Submit a role matrix, endpoint inventory and coverage sheet.
Write two validated findings and one secure-control verification.
Demonstrate a retest after an instructor-provided fix.

All testing takes place on assigned authorised labs with synthetic data.

Academy completion certificate only. No employment guarantee.
